steps.title: Lend it or own it
steps.body: Saving keeps money safe and ready. Investing puts it to work for years. There are two main ways. With a [[bond]], you lend money and get interest back. With a [[stock]], you own a small piece of a company. Its value goes up and down with the company. A fund such as an [[etf]] holds hundreds of them at once. More ups and downs usually come with more expected growth. They need time, so your [[time-horizon]] matters.

stat.label: main ways to invest: lend your money, or own a piece

steps.prompt: Match each place for money with what it is.
pairs: A small piece of one company
One fund holding hundreds of companies

steps.prompt: €10,000 can wait 20 years. Pick where it waits, then watch the 20 years go by.

choices.label: Savings account
choices.ending: €13,500. It never fell, not even for a day. But at 1.5% a year, it barely kept up with rising prices.

choices.label: A fund of bonds
choices.ending: €18,100. Small dips along the way, and steadier growth than savings.

choices.label: A world fund of stocks
choices.ending: €38,700, the most growth. But in year 8 it fell by almost a third. Only someone who could wait got the rest of the line.

steps.prompt: When will you need this money? Swipe each goal to the left or to the right.

items.text: Rent if you lose your job
A new laptop if yours breaks

steps.explanation: Money with a long [[time-horizon]] can sit out the ups and downs. Money for the next months cannot.

steps.prompt: Which of these usually swings the most in value from year to year?
steps.explanation: A [[stock]] moves with the company and the market. A savings account does not swing at all, and bonds usually swing less than stocks.

steps.prompt: Your investments are down 20% this month. Then your car breaks down. What happens if the money for the repair is in your investments?
options: You must sell them at a low price to pay for the repair
The bank pays you what they were worth before
Nothing, because losses only count at the end of the year
steps.explanation: You would sell at a low price and make the fall a real loss. That is why money for the next months stays out of investments.

steps.title: Where your money works
steps.body: You have **{savingsBalance}** in savings and **{depotTotal}** in your investment account. Each month, **{monthlyInvesting}** goes into a savings plan. The savings are ready any day. The investments are for later.

steps.title: Your decision
steps.body: Your investment account holds **{depotTotal}**. How many years can this money wait before you need it? You choose. The answer shapes how much up and down you can sit out.
steps.bodyNoData: How many years could invested money wait before you need it? You choose. The answer shapes how much up and down you can sit out.

rule.label: Years my invested money can wait
